title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array I
problemStatement: Search for a target in a rotated sorted array of distinct values.
intuition: A rotation splits the array into two sorted runs. At any mid, at least one side is fully sorted — check whether the target lies inside that sorted side, and discard accordingly.

approaches.title: Brute: linear scan
Optimal: modified binary search
approaches.idea: Compare a[lo] <= a[mid] to find the sorted half.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[4,5,6,7,0,1,2] t=0
mid=3 (7) left sorted [4..7], 0 not inside -> lo=4
mid=5 (1) left [0,1] sorted, 0 in [0,1) -> hi=4
mid=4 -> found at 4
approaches.whyWorks: At most one rotation point exists, so it can live in only one of the two halves.

specialTechnique.title: Sorted-half test
specialTechnique.body: a[lo] <= a[mid] identifies the sorted side. Use <= (not <) so that a two-element window is classified correctly.

commonMistakes: Using strict < in the sorted-half test
Getting the inclusive/exclusive ends wrong in the range checks
patternRecognition: Rotated sorted arrays -> "which half is clean?" decision
followUps: With duplicates (#87) — worst case degrades to O(n)
Find the pivot first, then do two plain binary searches
interviewInsight: Drawing the two-run picture before coding prevents the range-check mistakes almost entirely.
